rationale: Start with a broad mid-temperature scouting gradient to reveal the full elution window and avoid missing late compounds. This should show whether peaks are compressed early, eluting during the gradient, or still retained into the hold so the next runs can trim the window and adjust slope.

All 8 peaks are already within 10 minutes, so the only problem is the unresolved 4/5 pair; doubling tG isolates whether that pair responds to gradient slope. Keeping phi0, phi1, and T fixed preserves the elution window while making the gradient much shallower.

The 40 min run shows full resolution is possible, so now trim the gradient window to the actual elution band to keep those peaks inside a shallower, more selective region without paying the long run-time penalty. Centering the window around the observed elution zone should preserve separation of the critical pair while pulling t_last back toward 10 minutes.

The broad-window runs suggest the critical selectivity problem is a close pair that slope can fix only at a large time cost, so the next lever is temperature. Drop to 25 C while keeping the successful broad 20 min gradient to test whether modest selectivity changes can resolve that pair without pushing t_last past 10 minutes.

At 25 C the only remaining loss is slight under-resolution of one pair plus a small time penalty, so make the gradient just a bit steeper to pull t_last back toward 10 min while checking whether that pair stays near the threshold. This is a local optimization around the current best method.

The 18 min run showed the critical pair is very slope-sensitive, so step slightly shallower than the best 20 min method to try to push that pair above 1.5 while keeping the time penalty small. This is the most direct refinement around the current optimum.

The optimum is between the 20 min broad gradient at 25 C and 40 C, so raise temperature one step from the current best to reduce t_last while testing whether the critical pair remains close enough to full resolution. This targets a better balance of selectivity and run time than either 25 C or 40 C gave.

Keep the successful 25 C and 20 min slope, but slightly narrow the high-organic end because all peaks elute well before the gradient ends; this makes the effective gradient shallower in the occupied elution region. The goal is to gain a bit of resolution on the critical pair without lengthening the run as much as increasing tG to 22 min did.

Since temperature below 25 C is unavailable, probe slightly shallower than 22 min at the best temperature to see whether the critical pair gains enough margin to justify the extra retention. This maps the local tradeoff more finely around the current optimum.

The narrowed window at phi1 0.90 fully resolved all pairs but paid too much in retention, so make that window slightly steeper by shortening tG to 18 min. This tests whether full resolution can be preserved while bringing t_last back closer to 10 min and potentially surpassing the current best CRF.

A modestly narrower window improved the critical pair but retained peaks longer, so trim phi1 one more step while keeping the faster 18 min gradient to target a shallower effective slope specifically in the occupied region. This may lift the last weak pair above 1.5 with only a small additional time penalty.

Injection 11 is very close to ideal, with only a tiny resolution deficit in one pair, so make the gradient one step shallower at the same narrowed window. This should nudge that pair above 1.5 while keeping the time penalty modest enough to test for a new best CRF.

Now that the best window is near phi1 0.85, raise phi0 one step to remove unused low-organic range and steepen the early part less disproportionately in the occupied window. This could preserve the improved critical-pair selectivity while shortening the run enough to gain CRF.

You now have full resolution with only a tiny time penalty, so the next move is to shorten the gradient one step at the same window and temperature. This tests whether the critical pair can stay at or above 1.5 while pulling t_last to 10 minutes or less for a near-ideal score.

Keep the successful 18 min, 25 C method but trim phi1 one more step to make the effective gradient slightly shallower in the active region while also potentially shifting late peaks earlier under the lower hold composition balance. This is a close-in refinement around the current best full-resolution method.

The best method is very close to the time target, so raise phi0 one more step while keeping the proven 18 min and phi1 0.85 conditions to compress the early unused region and shorten retention. This tests whether the critical pair stays resolved while t_last moves to 10.0 minutes or below.

You have already reached the maximum CRF of 1.000, so further runs are only exploratory. Raising phi0 one more step tests how much safety margin remains in the optimum by shortening the method further while watching whether the critical 3/4 pair drops below 1.5.

Since increasing phi0 alone hurt the critical pair, test lowering phi1 one step from the optimum while keeping phi0 at 0.15 to see whether a slightly narrower window preserves full resolution and still stays under 10 minutes. This is the remaining nearby variant most likely to match the max score with a different robustness profile.

You already have a max-score method, so use the remaining budget to see whether this equally successful narrower window can be shortened one more step without losing full resolution. If it fails, it confirms 18 min is the shortest robust setting in this neighborhood.

With two max-score methods in hand, probe one more step narrower at the high end to test robustness and possibly identify the tightest fully resolving window. This keeps the proven 18 min slope while checking whether phi1 can be lowered without sacrificing the critical pair or pushing the last peak past 10 minutes.

Bracket the optimum from the other side by widening phi1 one step above the 0.85 maximum-score method while keeping phi0 and tG fixed. This confirms whether the best region is truly centered around 0.80–0.85 and gives a robustness comparison for the late-eluting pair.

The 0.15–0.80 window gave a max score at 18 min with ample margin on the worst pair, so try a slightly shallower version to map robustness of that method family. This checks whether it stays fully resolved and quantifies the tradeoff versus the already optimal 18 min setting.

Use the remaining runs to complete the local map around the two max-score methods by combining the higher phi0 with the stronger 0.80 upper limit. This tests whether the extra selectivity margin seen at phi1 0.80 can offset the loss in the critical pair caused by raising phi0.

Now push one more step higher in phi0 from the new max-score method to find the edge of failure and identify the shortest, strongest-start window that still fully resolves the mixture. This is the most informative remaining local test around the best-performing family.

For the final run, test the remaining nearby combination between the max-score methods at 0.20/0.80 and the fully resolved but slower 0.15/0.75. This checks whether a slightly higher phi0 with the narrower upper limit still keeps the critical pair above 1.5 while staying comfortably under 10 minutes.
